question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the **exact** values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x)={x}^{2}-4x$ on the interval $[0,3]$ are

$c=$
{{field-1}} $\,$ and $\,c=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3-0}{\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}-4x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{3}\cdot (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2})|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}-2\cdot {3}^{2})-(\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}-2\cdot {0}^{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot [(9-18)-(0-0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-9) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =-3 \\ {c}^{2}-4c & =-3 \\ {c}^{2}-4c+3 & =0 \\ (c-2)^{2}-1 & =0 \\ c-2 & =\pm 1 \\ c & =1,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem on the interval $[0,3]$ are 

$$
c=1,\,\text{and}\,c=3.
$$
